definition: The kind of a value, which decides what you can do with it. JavaScript's basic types include number, string, boolean, undefined and null; the typeof operator reports a value's type.
A name that points at a value so a program can use it later. In JavaScript the value has a type, not the variable, so one variable can point at different types over time.
The two modern ways to declare a variable. A const name can never be pointed at another value; a let name can be reassigned. Default to const and use let only when needed.
A number stored in binary with limited precision, as all JavaScript numbers are. Many decimals cannot be stored exactly, so 0.1 + 0.2 gives 0.30000000000000004; store money as whole cents instead.
A comparison that is true only when both values have the same type and the same value. Unlike loose equality (==), it never converts types first, so "5" === 5 is false.
A string written with backticks that can insert the value of any expression with ${ } and can span several lines, such as `Total: ${total}`.
How JavaScript treats any value used as a condition. Eight values are falsy: false, 0, -0, 0n, the empty string, null, undefined and NaN. Every other value is truthy.
A named, reusable block of code. It declares parameters, receives arguments when called, runs its body and hands a result back with return; without return the result is undefined.
A shorter function syntax, such as (cents) => cents / 100. With a single expression after the arrow, that expression is returned automatically; with curly braces, an explicit return is needed.
A function passed to another function, which decides when to call it. Array methods like map, event listeners and timers all take callbacks.
The region of code where a name can be used. let and const are scoped to the nearest block, and name lookups go outward from inner scopes to outer ones, never inward.
A function together with the variables from the scope where it was created. The function keeps access to them even after the outer function has returned, which gives it private, remembered state.
An ordered list of values, written in square brackets and indexed from 0. Arrays have methods such as map, filter, find and reduce for transforming and searching their items.
A value that groups named properties, such as { label: "Coffee", amount: 450 }. Properties are read with dot notation, or with brackets when the name is in a variable.
What a variable holds for an object or array: a pointer to it, not a copy. Assigning or passing it shares the same object, so a change through one name is visible through all.
Three dots that copy the items of an array or the properties of an object into a new one, as in [...list, item] or { ...expense, amount: 500 }. The copy is shallow.
Syntax that unpacks properties or array items into variables in one step, such as const { label, amount } = expense. It supports default values and works in function parameters.
An array method that walks the items while carrying an accumulator, returning the final accumulator. Used for totals and grouping; always pass an initial value as its second argument.
An operator that reads a property only if the value on its left is not null or undefined, returning undefined instead of throwing a TypeError, as in expense.receipt?.url.
An operator that returns its right side only when the left side is null or undefined. Unlike ||, it keeps real values such as 0 and the empty string.

The Document Object Model: the browser's live tree of objects representing the page. Changing these objects with JavaScript, for example an element's textContent, updates what the user sees immediately.

Handling events for many child elements with one listener on their container. Events bubble up to the container, and event.target.closest() finds which child was involved, including children added later.
JavaScript Object Notation, a text format for data. JSON.stringify turns values into JSON text and JSON.parse turns it back; it holds strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays and plain objects.
An object standing for a result that is not ready yet. It starts pending and settles once, either fulfilled with a value or rejected with an error; then and catch attach what happens next.

Syntax for working with promises. Inside an async function, await pauses that function until a promise settles and gives its value, so asynchronous code reads top to bottom and errors are caught with try/catch.
The mechanism that lets single-threaded JavaScript wait without freezing. When the call stack is empty, it runs all queued promise callbacks (microtasks), then the next task such as a timer or click.
A JavaScript file with its own scope that shares values with other files only through export and import. In the browser, the entry module is loaded with script type="module".
A blueprint for objects that bundles data with the methods that act on it. new runs the constructor and returns an instance; private fields marked with # are hidden from outside code.
The list of function calls, with file names and line numbers, that led to an error, most recent first. It shows where the error happened and how the program got there.
A marker in DevTools, or a debugger statement in code, that pauses execution on a line so you can inspect every variable, the call stack, and step through the code one line at a time.
